content.content: 1 using System.Text.Encodings.Web; 2 using System.Text.Json; 3 4 namespace Guardrails.Core.Graph; 5 6 /// 7 /// Renders the local-viewing companion to diagram.md: a self-contained 8 /// diagram.html that displays the SAME Mermaid DAG with pan / zoom / fullscreen, so a 9 /// large task+guardrail graph is actually navigable on disk (GitHub renders diagram.md 10 /// but offers no navigation). Pure: maps the rendered Mermaid text + its source-sha256 11 /// to an HTML string with no I/O (issue #33). 12 /// 13 /// 14 /// 15 /// The Mermaid source is embedded VERBATIM as the text content of a 16 /// <script type="text/plain"> element and read back via textContent — never 17 /// interpolated into a JS string. This sidesteps every escaping hazard (a label containing a 18 /// backtick, ${, or a quote cannot break the page), and a <script> element's 19 /// content is "raw text" so entities are not decoded — the source round-trips byte-for-byte. 20 /// This is safe because HTML-escapes every label (so < 21 /// becomes <), meaning the source can never contain </script>. 22 /// 23 /// 24 /// The source-sha256 provenance comment is emitted as the FIRST line (before 25 /// <!doctype html>) so the same \A-anchored reader that validates 26 /// diagram.md validates this file too (graph --check). A comment before the 27 /// doctype does not trigger quirks mode. 28 /// 29 /// 30 /// The renderer (Mermaid) and pan-zoom library load from a CDN, so the interactive view needs 31 /// internet the first time. GitHub will not execute the embedded script — this file is the 32 /// LOCAL artifact; diagram.md remains the portal artifact. Fully offline (inlined assets) 33 /// is a possible follow-up. 34 /// 35 /// 36 /// Legend overlay. A corner-anchored #legend <div> 37 /// (position: fixed), mirroring the existing #bar/#hint overlay divs, renders 38 /// 's content OUTSIDE the Mermaid SVG. A Mermaid-native 39 /// legend (a disconnected subgraph of colour-swatch nodes) was prototyped and rendered BROKEN — 40 /// dagre lays out a disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra "task" overlapping the real DAG — so 41 /// the overlay div is the only approach that renders correctly. Static HTML, not templated from 42 /// the Mermaid source, so it carries no bearing on source-sha256. 43 /// 44 /// 45 /// Task-container click target: a POST-RENDER SVG title-band overlay (issue #232/#233 46 /// superseded, issue #235). A Mermaid click directive never fires on a subgraph/cluster 47 /// element (upstream limitation; see remarks), and the first fix 48 /// attempt — an invisible anchor NODE inside the container — proved useless in practice: dagre 49 /// sizes and packs it into whatever gap its own layout leaves, which for a content-dense container 50 /// is a tiny, off-center sliver (measured: 0.44% of the container's area on a real 4-guardrail 51 /// task). The fix implemented here instead runs AFTER mermaid.render resolves: for every 52 /// g.cluster element whose id starts with task_, compute a full-width band from the 53 /// cluster's own bounding box down to just past its .cluster-label's bottom edge (Mermaid 54 /// always reserves this header strip above any leaf content, so it is empty BY CONSTRUCTION 55 /// regardless of how many guardrails/preflights the task has — unlike an interior anchor node) and 56 /// append a real <a href="..." target="_blank"><rect fill="transparent"></a> 57 /// spanning it. APPENDED, not inserted first: a cluster's only two original children are its 58 /// background <rect> then its .cluster-label group, so appending puts the 59 /// overlay last in paint order (on top, clickable) without moving in front of the label text 60 /// visually (the rect is transparent) and — because every leaf check node lives in an entirely 61 /// separate top-level SVG group from its own container's g.cluster — the overlay can never 62 /// occlude or be occluded by a leaf node's own click target either way. The task→folder-path data 63 /// this script needs () is embedded as a small JSON 64 /// object keyed by the SAME container id the Mermaid source uses, in a 65 /// <script type="application/json"> element read back via textContent (same 66 /// verbatim/never-interpolated treatment as the Mermaid source itself, immune to the same escaping 67 /// hazards). 68 /// 69 /// 70 /// Long task-name title wrap-overflow, fixed by widening the label's foreignObject 71 /// post-render (issue cluster-label-wrap-overflow). Mermaid always wraps a cluster's title 72 /// <div> to a hardcoded 200px width (the bundled mermaid@11.4.1's plain 73 /// flowchart cluster shape never overrides createText's width = 200 default, 74 /// regardless of the container's own — usually much wider — computed width), and dagre's layout 75 /// pass reserves the container's header-strip height BEFORE that wrapped height is known, so a 76 /// long kebab-case task name (hyphens are valid soft line-break points) that wraps to 2+ lines 77 /// prints past the reserved strip, overlapping the first leaf guardrail/preflight box positioned 78 /// directly below. No Mermaid config knob avoids this — flowchart.htmlLabels only toggles 79 /// the html-vs-svg-text label renderer, and 11.4.1 has no documented option for cluster-label 80 /// wrap width. The fix (the fixWrappedClusterLabels function, run AFTER 81 /// mermaid.render resolves and BEFORE the title-band overlay above, since the overlay's 82 /// band height depends on the label's — by then possibly shrunk — bounding box) re-wraps the 83 /// SAME text at up to the container's own width instead: since the container is normally already 84 /// wider than 200px, this almost always drops the label to one line, which needs LESS height than 85 /// the original wrap — never more — so no other node/edge/container ever needs to move. Verified 86 /// headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names): every wrapped case converged to one line 87 /// with the same healthy gap a never-wrapped label already has, and every already-fits label 88 /// (including the whole golden hello-guardrails example) was left byte-for-byte unchanged. 89 /// 90 /// 91 public static class HtmlDiagramRenderer 92 { 93 /// 94 /// Build the diagram.html document for (the exact 95 /// text rendered into diagram.md, including the flowchart TD header and the 96 /// cosmetic classDef lines) stamped with . is the task-container-id → plan-relative-folder-path map (see 98 /// ) the embedded title-band overlay script uses 99 /// to resolve each container's click target (issue #235 — see class remarks). 100 /// 101 /// 102 /// OPTIONAL live-run status map (issue #219): Mermaid node/container id → one of 103 /// "pending", "running", "passed", "failed", "needs-human", 104 /// keyed by the SAME ids emits (task containers task_<base>, 105 /// preflight/guardrail leaves task_<base>_pf_<n>/task_<base>_gr_<n>, 106 /// and the plan-level brackets plan_preflights/plan_guardrails). When non-null the 107 /// document additionally carries a per-node status-overlay badge (an animated spinner while 108 /// running, a settled check/X/"?" glyph once finished). When null (the static 109 /// graph command, which never runs live) the output is byte-identical to the pre-#219 110 /// three-argument render. 111 /// 112 /// 113 /// INDEPENDENT of the status overlay (mirrors LogSiteRenderer.IndexHtml(..., includeRefresh)): 114 /// when is non-null AND this is true (the default, 115 /// the DURING-RUN diagram) a <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="2"> is emitted so a 116 /// plain file:// view re-reads itself as the run progresses; when false (the FINAL 117 /// settled render wired at run-end by 06-wire-diagramobserver-into-runcommand) the overlay 118 /// is still emitted but the refresh tag is not. Ignored when is null. 119 /// 120 public static string Render( 121 string mermaidSource, string sourceHash, IReadOnlyDictionary taskFolderTargets, 122 IReadOnlyDictionary? nodeStatuses = null, bool includeRefresh = true) 123 { 124 ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(mermaidSource); 125 ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrEmpty(sourceHash); 126 ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(taskFolderTargets); 127 128 // Newline-normalize so the file is byte-identical across OSes (mirrors the renderer/hash). 129 string source = mermaidSource 130 .Replace("\r\n", "\n", StringComparison.Ordinal) 131 .Replace("\r", "\n", StringComparison.Ordinal) 132 .TrimEnd('\n'); 133 134 // Encoder that escapes NOTHING beyond what JSON strictly requires (default System.Text.Json 135 // escapes '<', '>', '&', etc. as \uXXXX for HTML safety, which is unnecessary here — the 136 // JSON sits inside a \n" 215 + " 389 390 391 591 592 593 """; 594 } 595
